deities: Sri Uma Markandeyeswara Swamy (Shiva lingam, 3-ft black marble, per pilgrimaide)

history.dynasty: Eastern Chalukya origin; patronage by Raja Raja Narendra, Cholas and Reddy Rajas; reconstructed 1818 by Gundu Sobhanadriswara Rao
history.period: 10th century AD origin (per velpu.com, wanderlog); present structure 1818 onward
history.summary: Sri Uma Markandeyeswara Swamy Temple is an ancient Shiva temple on the Godavari bund road near Pushkar Ghat Circle, Rajahmundry, whose lingam is traditionally said to have been installed by the sage Markandeya. Sources (velpu.com, wanderlog) trace it to the Eastern Chalukyas in the 10th century AD with later Chola and Reddy patronage. Per velpu.com it was demolished during Muslim rule and rediscovered in 1818 in the relics of a dilapidated mosque near Chanda Choultry, then rebuilt by Gundu Sobhanadriswara Rao (hence access via Gunduvari Street). The main shrine is about 10 feet below current road level with a 5-tier east-facing rajagopuram. The legend: sage Mrukhanada's son Markandeya, doomed to die at age 11, embraced the lingam and was rescued from Yama by Shiva. CSV town 'Rajahmundry' is correct.

name: Sri Uma Markandeyeswara Swamy Temple
town_description: Rajahmundry (officially Rajamahendravaram) is a historic city on the eastern bank of the Godavari River in coastal Andhra Pradesh, often called the cultural capital of the state. Founded around the 11th century by the Eastern Chalukyas (Raja Raja Narendra), it was the first capital of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty and later the birthplace of the Telugu language's classical literature. Today it is a major rail and road hub with its own airport, and its river ghats (Gowthami, Pushkar) are among the busiest pilgrimage spots on the Godavari.

travel.airport: Rajahmundry Airport (approx. 15-18 km; limited domestic flights) (verify); Vijayawada Airport (approx. 160 km) for wider connectivity.
travel.railway: Rajahmundry Junction, a major station on the Howrah-Chennai main line, a few km away; autos/cabs to Godavari Bund Road.
travel.road: The temple is on Godavari Bund Road near Pushkar Ghat Circle (plus code 2Q38+4XJ per wanderlog), reachable by auto, cab or city bus from anywhere in Rajahmundry.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Mahasivarathri and Kartika Masam are the busiest pilgrim seasons.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM to 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM daily per pilgrimaide (one other source, velpu.com, says 5:00 AM to 8:00 PM - verify). Modest dress; many devotees bathe in the Godavari before entering.
